purpose: A change to how the LIVE book trades must be DECLARED before it ships. This file is the declaration. It records the configuration currently in force, and every change to it, with the reason and the evidence. If the measured fingerprint does not match declared_fingerprint, the guard fails and the deploy is blocked.
why: The forward record is the only evidence that can ever defeat deflation: a pre-registered book run forward is N=1, so its hurdle is 0.88 Sharpe at five years against 2.44 for a backtest selected from 162 identities. That record is fourteen days old and it is the most valuable asset in the project. A live configuration change silently contaminates it, and until this file existed nothing stood in the way of one -- there were 85 checks around admitting a sleeve and none around re-sizing the whole book.

the_incident_this_exists_for.what: cov_halflife_bars (default 720) was changed to cov_halflife_days (default 21). No call site passes that argument, the walk-forwards are regenerated by the daily ticks, and live_cycle.py submits the last leg's weights to the broker -- so the change would have re-sized two broker-executed sleeves on the next tick. The commit said 'nothing was re-run'. Reverted the same day after an adversarial audit.
the_incident_this_exists_for.the_rule_it_produced: A DEFAULT NOBODY OVERRIDES IS NOT A DEFAULT, IT IS THE PRODUCTION SETTING. Before changing one, grep for who passes it; if nobody does, you are changing the live book.

how_to_change_the_live_book: 1. Measure the change on the LIVE path, not a simulation of it. The overlay halflife was priced against an untruncated EWMA the production estimator is not (artifacts/analysis/live_covariance_memory).
2. Write the reason and the evidence path into change_log below.
4. Expect the forward record to be marked at that date. A change is a new specification, and the record before it and after it are not the same experiment.

change_log.reason: Establishes the baseline against which future changes are detected. The configuration recorded here is the one the book has been running since the v3 re-baseline on 2026-08-07.
